Jo-An Occhipinti <jo-an.occhipinti@sydney.edu.au>:
Hi Sara, I have spent most of the morning attempting to use the app as if I was a participant. There are a few more minor things I think should be refined for the demographic module some of which I can do myself with the researcher access (the rest I can summaries in a subsequent email). The mental health and community connection modules and quick and easy to use so all good there. Unfortunately the Social Production module simply isn’t satisfactory. • The first question that appears when I go into the social production app is ‘Which activity best describes how you spent this time? (what time? This sounds like a follow up question but it is the first question that appears and participants will be confused). • This question lists activities to select from, asks you for a time period (which is confusing when I chose the work activity as the time period I entered was the whole period because I work every day (but then I had to go back and correct this when I understood I needed to choose a period of one day only). • It then asked me where was I when I did this activity, who I was with, unpaid overtime, whether my profession was in the arts, then thanked me for my contribution to understanding mental wealth and directed me to submit (which seemed strange as it felt like the end of the survey). • Only when I pressed submit button did a diary appear….and it didn’t default to the date that I had entered the activity for, I had to go looking for it. When I found the activity and was done editing the time period, it went back to the home page which meant I had to go back into the survey to enter the next activity (some people may not enter again thinking they may have completed the survey. • On the diary page I can’t click on a time and have a selection of activities come up and modify the time by clicking and dragging like in a normal iphone diary. • The whole experience was very complex, non-intuitive, and will frustrate participants, likely resulting in responses that will be incomplete and there will be high disengagement with the survey/app. • Are you able to use the app as if you are a participant and see if the module works differently / is intuitive to use for you? I’m not sure whether something is wrong with the module, or the module just on my phone. Please note I am using an iPhone 8 with iOS 16.7.10. Can we set up a meeting to discuss/reconfigure this module asap if it is indeed not just a problem with my phone app? Many thanks, Jo Jo-An Occhipinti (née Atkinson) | Associate Professor Co-Director, Mental Wealth Initiative Head, Systems Modelling & Simulation Brain and Mind Centre | Youth Mental Health and Technology Faculty of Medicine and Health | Translational Research Collective The University of Sydney Level 5 | Moore College CG2 | 1 King Street, NEWTOWN | NSW | 2042 jo-an.occhipinti@sydney.edu.au | sydney.edu.au/bmri Mental Wealth: https://www.sydney.edu.au/brain-mind/our-research/mental-wealth-initiative.html AI research: https://ai-research.csart-world.com/ Twitter: @JM_Occhipinti | LinkedIn: @Jo-An_Occhipinti We acknowledge the tradition of custodianship and law of the Country on which the University of Sydney campuses stand.
